"As if the gazelles of al-Mukhaymar at dawn, from the flood and the debris, were a spindle whorl."

"A honey-lipped beloved with a dark-greenish tint on her lips, and in her gums and her front teeth a sweet brightness."

It has also been said that it is a greenness with blackness over it. (Al-ahwā) is the gazelle that has two dark and white lines on its back. The poet said:

"Among the tribe is a dark-spotted young gazelle shaking off the dew, glossy, between two strands of pearl and emerald."

﴿But the most wretched will avoid it﴾, meaning the one who is ﴿the most wretched﴾, that is, the one who is extreme in wretchedness, because the disbeliever in the Messenger (ﷺ) is the most wretched of the disbelievers, just as the believer in him and in what he brought is the best of those who believed in any messenger before him. Then He described him with what his state will lead to in the Hereafter, namely the burning of the Fire, and He described it as ﴿the greatest﴾. Al-Hasan said: "The greatest Fire is the Fire of the Hereafter, and the lesser is the Fire of this world." Al-Farra' said: "The greatest is the lowest of the layers of the Fire." It has also been said: the Fire of the Hereafter varies in degree, so within it is something greater than something else.

﴿Then he will neither die﴾ and thus find rest, ﴿nor live﴾ a pleasant life. The particle *thumma* (then), which implies delay, is used to signal the varying degrees of severity, because wavering between life and death is more intense and more dreadful than being burned in the Fire.

﴿Indeed, he has succeeded﴾, meaning he has prospered and attained his aim, ﴿who purifies himself﴾, meaning who purifies himself. Ibn Abbas said: "From polytheism, and he says: There is no god but Allah." Al-Hasan said: "Whoever's deed is pure." Abu al-Ahwas, Qatada, and a group said: "Whoever gives charity from his wealth and pays zakat."

﴿And remembers the name of his Lord﴾, meaning he affirms His oneness and does not associate anything with Him as a rival, ﴿and prays﴾, meaning he performs the obligatory prayer and whatever voluntary prayers (nawafil) he is able to. The meaning is that when he remembers, he believes in Allah. Then He informed about Himself, may He be exalted, that whoever brings these two acts of worship, prayer and zakat, has succeeded. He used His saying ﴿and remembers the name of his Lord﴾ as evidence that the opening takbir (takbirat al-ifitah) is obligatory, and that it is permissible to use any of His names, and that it is not part of the prayer, because the prayer is coordinated with the remembrance, which is the opening takbir. This is a weak argument. Ibn Abbas said: "﴿And remembers the name of his Lord﴾" means his return and his standing before his Lord, so he prays to Him.

The majority of reciters read ﴿But you prefer﴾ with the second-person ta' (taa' al-khitab), addressing the disbelievers. It has also been said that it is addressed to both the righteous and the wicked: the righteous prefer it to acquire reward, and the wicked out of their desire for it. ʿAbd Allah, Abu Raja', al-Hasan, al-Jahdari, Abu Hayawa, Ibn Abi ʿAbla, Abu ʿAmr, al-Zaʿfarani, and Ibn Miqsam read it with the third-person ya' (ya' al-ghayba). ﴿Indeed, this﴾, meaning the report of the success of him who purifies himself and of people's preference for this world, as said by Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir. This is preferred because of the proximity of what is referred to by "this." Ibn Abbas, ʿIkrima, and al-Suddi said it refers to the meanings of the sura. al-Dahhak said it refers to the Qur'an. Qatada said it refers to His saying: ﴿But the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾.

The success of him who purifies himself and that ﴿the Hereafter is better and more lasting﴾ have not been abrogated (nuskh) in any of the sharia laws; rather, they are in the former scriptures and in the final sharia. Ibn Khalawayh said: "*Ibrahim* has also been read with an alif and a ḍamma on the hāʾ," meaning *Ibrahum*. The discussion of the scrolls of Ibrahim and Musa, upon them be blessings and peace, has already been covered under *al-Najm*.

This includes the comprehensiveness of His knowledge of all things.

It has also been said that it means the easy, upright Sharia (al-shari'a al-hanifiyya). It has also been said that it means He will lead you to good matters in your worldly affairs and your Hereafter, such as victory, high station, and elevation in Paradise.
